market_question: Will France send warships through the Strait of Hormuz by May 31, 2026?
reasoning: France is a key contributor to the European Maritime Awareness in the Strait of Hormuz (EMASoH) mission, which regularly deploys warships to escort merchant vessels through the Strait. Given a 1.5-year window, it is very likely at least one French frigate will transit and be officially confirmed or credibly reported. The market significantly underestimates this routine operational tempo.
evidence_points: France has continuously participated in EMASoH, with warships like FS La Fayette and FS Courbet deployed to the region in 2023–2024.
Rotational deployments typically last several months, making transits through the Strait a near-certainty within the timeframe.
Even without official announcements, overwhelming credible media reporting would resolve the market; naval movements in the Strait are well-monitored.
sources_consulted: EMASoH official mission overview (European-led maritime surveillance)
Public records of French Navy frigate deployments to the Gulf (e.g., FS La Fayette in 2023, FS Courbet in 2024)
News articles on France’s naval presence in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz
